Rashi on Shabbat 86a:1:1.english: Like a square board - Thus, a round [one] is not a garden bed.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:1:2.hebrew: התם - דבעי מרובעת לאחשובה שדה, קאמר להתיר ראש תור כו'. ולית ליה לר' יוחנן הא דאמר לעיל "אין ראש תור בערוגה"? אי נמי, אית ליה מערוגה לערוגה, אבל משדה לערוגה יש ראש תור:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:1:2.english: There - [where the baraita] requires [the garden bed to be] square in order to give it the status of a field, it states [this] to permit a triangular protrusion, etc. And does R. Yochanan not hold [the principle] that he stated above, "There is no [leniency of] a triangular protrusion in a garden bed"? Alternatively, he holds [that it does not apply] from one garden bed to another garden bed, whereas from a field to a garden bed there is [a leniency of] a triangular protrusion.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:1.hebrew: שהיא טמאה - דיום השלישי אכתי לא מסרחה שכבת זרע, וראויה לקלוט ולהיות ולד נוצר הימנה, וקרינן שכבת זרע הראוי להזריע:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:1.english: That she is impure - For [on] the third day the semen has not yet putrefied, and it is fit to conceive and for an embryo to be formed from it, and we call [it] semen fit to inseminate.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:2.hebrew: לג' ימים - דהקפיד הכתוב על טומאת קרי במתן תורה, וקס"ד עם יום הפרישה קאמר, דבד' בשבת פירשו מנשותיהן וקבלו תורה בשבת, שהוא רביעי לאותם ששימשו מטותיה' ברביעי לפני הפרישה, וטבלו לילי שבת. ולא חש הכתוב אם יפלוטו בשבת, דמסרח ואינו שכבת זרע הראוי להזריע; אבל אם פלטו ע"ש בשלישי — טמאות, לכך הפרישן שלשה ימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:2.english: For three days - For Scripture was particular about the ritual impurity of a seminal emission at the giving of the Torah, and [the Tanna] initially assumed that [Moses] meant [three days] inclusive of the day of separation: that on Wednesday they separated from their wives and received the Torah on Shabbat, which is the fourth [day] for those who had marital relations on Wednesday before the separation, and they immersed on Friday night. And Scripture was not concerned if they would discharge [semen] on Shabbat, because it has decomposed and is no longer semen fit to fertilize; however, if they discharged on Friday, on the third [day], they would be ritually impure — therefore [Moses] separated them for three days.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:3.hebrew: מנין שמרחיצין - דאף ביום ג' מסוכן הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:3.english: From where [is it derived] that one may wash [the circumcision] - For even on the third day he is in danger.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:2:4.english: Like water into his inward parts and like oil into his bones - [The verse] compares anointing to drinking.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:1.english: The first clause - of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:2.hebrew: דלא כר' אלעזר בן עזריה - דאילו לדידי' שמעינן ליה פולטת ביום השלישי טהורה, לקמן בברייתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:2.english: Is not in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya - For as for him, we have heard him [state that a woman] who discharges [semen] on the third day is ritually pure, [as taught] below in a baraita.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:3.hebrew: וסיפא - דקתני מרחיצין את המילה כו', ר' אלעזר בן עזריה, דהוא אמר לה לקמן בפרק ר' אליעזר:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:3.english: And the latter clause - Which teaches: "One may bathe the [infant after] circumcision," etc., [is in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, for he said it later in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:4.hebrew: מאן דלא מוקי כתנאי - דדחיק ומוקי מתניתין בתרי טעמי, או משבש לה ומפרש לה דלא לאוקמי כתנאי — משבש לה ואמר משבשתא היא, ותני בה טהורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:4.english: He who does not establish [the Mishnah] as [reflecting two] Tannaim - [That is, one] who forces and establishes our Mishnah with two [different] reasons, or emends it and explains it so as not to establish [it] as [reflecting two] Tannaim — [here] he emends it and says, "It is corrupted," and teaches in it "ritually pure."

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:5.hebrew: ומאן דמוקי לה כתנאי - דניחא ליה לאוקומי כתנאי מלמימר משבשתא היא ומלאוקמי בתרי טעמי, מוקי נמי להאי כתנאי. ופלוגתא היא בהמפקיד (ב"מ מא.) גבי חבית, דאמר ר' יוחנן: מאן דמתרגם לי חבית אליבא דחד תנא מובילנא ליה מאני לבי מסותא; ומוקי רישא ר' ישמעאל וסיפא רבי עקיבא, ואי הוה בעי הוה מצי לאוקמי בתרי טעמי ובחד תנא, ואיכא דמוקי לה התם בחד תנא, ומוקי סיפא בשהניחה במקום שאינו מקומה:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:3:5.english: And he who establishes it according to [two] Tannaim - Since it is preferable to him to establish [a Mishnah] according to [different] Tannaim rather than to say it is corrupt and rather than to establish it with two [different] reasons, he establishes this [Mishnah] as well according to [two] Tannaim. And this is a dispute in [the chapter] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 41a) regarding a barrel, where R' Yochanan said: "Whoever interprets [the Mishnah of] the barrel for me according to one Tanna, I will carry his clothes to the bathhouse!" And [one Amora] establishes the first clause [as] R' Yishmael and the latter clause [as] R' Akiva, even though if he had wanted, he could have established it with two [different] reasons and according to one Tanna; while there is [another Amora] who establishes it there according to one Tanna, and establishes the latter clause [as referring to a case] where he placed it in a place that is not its [proper] place.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:1.hebrew: ביום השלישי - כגון ששמשה בה' ופלטה שכבת זרע בשבת: ל"ש שמשה תחילת ליל חמישי, דאישתהי ד' עונות שלמות — ליל ה' וה', ליל ו' וו' — ל"ש שמשה יום ה' עם חשיכה, דלא אישתהי אלא מקצת ה' וליל ו' וו', דליכא אלא ב' עונות שלמות. העונה — או יום או לילה:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:1.english: On the third day - For example, [a case] where she had marital relations on Thursday and discharged semen on Shabbat: it makes no difference [whether] she had relations at the beginning of the eve of Thursday [Wednesday night], so that it remained [inside her] for four complete periods — the night of Thursday and Thursday [day], the night of Friday and Friday [day] — or [whether] she had relations on Thursday [day] at dusk, so that it remained only part of Thursday, the night of Friday, and Friday [day], so that there are only two complete periods. A period [is] either a day or a night.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:2.hebrew: ר' ישמעאל אומר פעמים שהן כו' - בא לחלוק ולומר דפולטת בג' לשימושה טמאה, אבל פולטת בד' טהורה. ומודינא לך דמקצת היום ככולו, דלא הקפידה תורה אלא במנין של הימים ולא במנין העונות:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:2.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: Sometimes there are, etc. - He comes to disagree and say that one who discharges [semen] on the third [day] from her marital relations is ritually impure, whereas one who discharges on the fourth [day] is ritually pure. And I concede to you that part of the day is like the whole [day], for the Torah was particular only about the count of the days, and not about the count of the [twelve-hour] periods.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:3.hebrew: ופעמים שהם ד' עונות - שלמות, שאם שמשה ד' בשבת עם חשיכה, פליטתה טמאה עד תחלת שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:3.english: And sometimes they are four periods - Complete [periods], for if she had marital relations on Wednesday at dusk, her discharge is ritually impure until the beginning of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:4.hebrew: פעמים שהם ה' עונות - כגון שמשה בתחלת היום של ד':
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:4.english: Sometimes there are five periods - For example, [when] she had marital relations at the beginning of the day of Wednesday.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:5.hebrew: פעמים שהן ו' - כגון שמשה בתחלת ליל ד', בין השמשות:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:5.english: Sometimes there are six [periods] - For example, [when] she had relations at the beginning of Wednesday night, at twilight.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:6.hebrew: נותנין לה מקצת עונת ו' - להשלים ה', וכל הפולטת בתוך ה' עונות שלמות טמאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:4:6.english: She is given part of the sixth period - To complete five [periods], and any [woman] who discharges within five complete periods is ritually impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:1.english: They said it - [They said] this objection that [follows] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:2.hebrew: בשלמא כו' - פלוגתא דרבנן ור' יוסי בברייתא, ומייתי לה בהאי פירקא לקמן, דלרבנן בה' בשבת פרשו, ולר' יוסי בד'. ולכ"ע בשבת ניתנו עשרת הדברות, וכיון דבשבת נתנו, ע"כ בליל שבת טבלו ולא שחרית, כדמתרץ לקמן: שלא יהו הללו טובלין והללו מהלכין לקבל תורה. הלכך, בשלמא ר' אלעזר כרבנן, דאמרי בחמשה בשבת עבוד פרישה, ויש שלא פרשו אלא עם חשיכה, ומדטבלו ליל שבת ולא חשו שמא תפלטנה עוד, ש"מ דפולטת בג' טהורה, ומקצת היום של תשמיש ככולו:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:2.english: Granted, etc. - [This refers to] a dispute between the Rabbis and Rabbi Yosei in a baraita, which [the Gemara] cites later in this chapter: according to the Rabbis they separated on the fifth day of the week [Thursday], and according to Rabbi Yosei on the fourth [Wednesday]. And according to all opinions, the Ten Commandments were given on Shabbat; and since they were given on Shabbat, perforce they immersed on Shabbat night [Friday night] and not in the morning — as [the Gemara] explains later, so that these should not be immersing while those are walking to receive the Torah. Therefore, granted Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya holds] in accordance with the Rabbis, who say they instituted separation on the fifth day of the week, and there were some who did not separate until nightfall; and since they immersed on Shabbat night and were not concerned lest they discharge [semen] again, learn from this that one who discharges on the third [day] is pure, and part of the day of intercourse is [reckoned] as the whole [day].

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:3.hebrew: ור' ישמעאל - דאומר בג' טמאה, בד' טהורה, קסבר בד' עבוד פרישה כר' יוסי, דהוה ליל שבת רביעי. ומיהו, יש שלא פירשו עד סמוך לחשיכה, וליכא אלא ד' עונות — ליל ה' וה', ליל ו' וו' — ואפילו הכי, משטבלו פליטתן טהורה, דלא הקפידה תורה אלא בימים:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:3.english: And Rabbi Yishmael - Who says [that] on the third [day] she is impure [and] on the fourth [day] she is pure, holds [that] on the fourth [day of the week] they instituted separation, in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, so that Shabbat eve was the fourth [day]. However, there were some who did not separate until close to nightfall, so there were only four twelve-hour periods — the night of the fifth [day] and the fifth [day], the night of the sixth [day] and the sixth [day] — and even so, once they immersed, their discharge is pure, for the Torah was particular only about days:

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:4.hebrew: אלא רבי עקיבא - דאמר כל ה' עונות טמאה אם תפלוט, כמאן? ומהיכא למד דאעונות קפיד קרא, הא ימים כתיב, וקיימא לן מקצת היום ככולו:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:4.english: However, Rabbi Akiva - who says [that for] all five onot [twelve-hour periods] she is impure if she discharges [semen], in accordance with whom [does he hold]? And from where did he learn that the verse is particular about onot, [when] "days" is written, and we maintain [that] part of a day is like an entire [day]?

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:5.hebrew: לעולם - ר' עקיבא כר' יוסי, וכדרב אדא דאמר: משה כל עליותיו בהשכמה עלה וכל ירידותיו בהשכמה. הלכך, ירידה דכתיב: "וירד משה מן ההר אל העם ויקדש את העם" — דהיינו פרישה — בהשכמת רביעי היתה; ומדהוזקק להפרישן בהשכמה, ש"מ עד ה' עונות שלמות קפיד קרא:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:5:5.english: Actually - Rabbi Akiva [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, and in accordance with Rav Adda, who said: Moses ascended [for] all his ascents early in the morning, and [descended for] all his descents early in the morning. Therefore, the descent of which it is written: "And Moses came down from the mountain to the people, and sanctified the people" — which refers to [marital] separation — was early in the morning of the fourth [day]; and since he was required to separate them early in the morning, learn from this [that] the verse is particular [to require] up to five complete [twelve-hour] periods.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:7:1.english: And we ask: Why did he need to tell them - In the morning, even without this, they would not have had relations.

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:7:2.hebrew: דקאמר רב הונא - דאין משמשין ביום, דכתיב (משלי י״ט:ט״ז) "בוזה דרכיו ימות", דבעי צניעותא שלא יסתכלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:7:2.english: That Rav Huna said - that they do not have relations during the day, as it is written (Proverbs 19:16), "He who despises his ways shall die," for it requires modesty, so that they do not look [at one another].

Rashi on Shabbat 86a:7:3.hebrew: תלמיד חכם - שהוא צנוע ולא יסתכל, סגי ליה במאפיל בטליתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 86a:7:3.english: A Torah scholar - Since he is modest and will not gaze, it is sufficient for him to darken [the space] with his cloak.

Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:2:1.hebrew: מנין לפולטת כו' שנא' היו נכונים לשלשת ימים - אע"פ שבאותה שעה עדיין לא ניתנה תורה, מ"מ מסתמא הקפידה תורה על דבר שעתיד להיות טומאה אחר מתן תורה. ואע"ג דלא הקפידה על זבין ומצורעין ובועלי נדות, היינו משום טעמא דתניא בפרק מי שמתו (ברכות כב.): "כתיב 'והודעתם לבניך ולבני בניך', וכתיב 'יום אשר עמדת לפני ה' אלהיך בחורב' — מה להלן באימה וביראה וברתת ובזיע כו', מכאן אמרו: זבין ומצורעים ובועלי נדות מותרין לקרות בתורה בנביאים ולשנות במשנה ובש"ס בהלכות ובאגדות, ובעלי קריין אסורין". פירוש: דבעל קרי אינו באימה וביראה, דמחמת קלות ראש הוא בא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:2:1.english: From where [is it derived] that [a woman] who discharges [semen], etc., as it is stated: "Prepare yourselves for three days" - Even though at that time the Torah had not yet been given, nevertheless, presumably the Torah was particular about something that would become [a source of] ritual impurity after the giving of the Torah. And even though [the Torah] was not particular about zavin [men with seminal-like emissions], and metzoraim [people with skin afflictions], and those who cohabit with menstruants, that is for the reason taught in a baraita in the chapter [entitled] Mi Shemeito (Berakhot 22a): "It is written: 'And you shall make them known to your children and your children's children,' and it is written: 'The day that you stood before the Lord your God at Horeb' — just as there [at Sinai] it was in awe, and in fear, and in trembling, and in sweat, etc., [so too here]. From here they said: Zavin, and metzoraim, and those who cohabit with menstruants are permitted to read in the Torah [and] in the Prophets, and to study in the Mishnah and in the Talmud, in halakhot and in aggadot, whereas those who experienced a seminal emission are forbidden." Explanation: For one who experienced a seminal emission is not in [a state of] awe and fear, since it comes about through lightheadedness.

Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:2:2.hebrew: אע"פ שאין ראייה לדבר זכר לדבר שנאמר ותבא כמים וגו' - ומיהו ראיה גמורה לא הוי, משום דקרא לא מישתעי בשתיה אלא ברחיצה, משום דמשמע מים דומיא דשמן — מה שמן מאבראי, אף מים מאבראי. וקשה לר"י, דבפרק בתרא דיומא (דף עו.) קאמר: "דרחיצה איקרי עינוי מנלן? א"ר זוטרא: מהכא, 'ותבא כמים בקרבו וגו'', מים דומיא דשמן — מה שמן מאבראי כו'". ופריך: "והא האי תנא איפכא נסיב לה, דתנן 'מנין לסיכה כו''"! ומאי פריך? הא תנא דמתני' קאמר שאין ראיה לדבר אלא זכר לדבר, משום דמים דומיא דשמן כדפרישי'! ואומר ר"י דפריך הכי: דאי חשיבא ראיה גמורה דרחיצה כסיכה כדקאמרת, לא הוה ליה להאי תנא למעבד מינה אפי' זכר בעלמא. קשה לרשב"א: דאמאי מייתי האי קרא שאינו אלא זכר בעלמא? הוה ליה לאיתויי קרא ד"לחם חמודות לא אכלתי ובשר ויין לא בא אל פי וסוך לא סכתי" (דניאל י׳:ג׳), דהוי דרשה גמורה, ומיניה נפקא לן בפרק בתרא דיומא (שם) דסיכה איקרי עינוי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:2:2.english: "Although there is no proof for this, there is an allusion to it, as it is stated: 'And it comes like water,' etc." - However, it is not a complete proof, because the verse is not speaking of drinking, but rather of washing, since it implies water is similar to oil — just as oil is [applied] externally, so too water is [applied] externally. And it is difficult for Rabbeinu Yitzchak, for in the last chapter of Yoma (76a) [the Gemara] says: "From where [do we derive] that washing is called affliction? Rav Zutra said: From here: 'And it comes into his inward parts like water,' etc. — water is similar to oil; just as oil is [applied] externally, etc." And [the Gemara] asks: "But this Tanna derives it in the opposite way, as we learned in the Mishnah: 'From where [is it derived] that smearing [is like drinking],' etc." Now, what is [the Gemara] asking? Surely the Tanna of our Mishnah says that there is no proof for this, only an allusion to it, because water is similar to oil as I explained! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that [the Gemara] is asking thus: If [the verse] is considered a complete proof that washing is like smearing, as you say, this Tanna should not have made even a mere allusion from it [to the opposite]. [Moreover,] it is difficult for the Rashba: Why does [the Mishnah] bring this verse, which is only a mere allusion? It should have brought the verse, "I ate no pleasant bread, neither came flesh nor wine into my mouth, neither did I smear myself at all" (Daniel 10:3), which is a complete exposition, and from it we derive in the last chapter of Yoma (ibid.) that smearing is called affliction.

Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:3:1.hebrew: תני רישא טהורה ומוקי לה כו' - אומר ר"י, דמשום הכי אינו מגיה למיתני "טהורה" כדי לאוקמי כולה כרבי אלעזר, אלא בלאו הכי איכא דתני "טהורה" ואיכא דתני "טמאה"; הלכך מאן דלא מוקי כתנאי — נוח לו לשנות כאותן ששונין "טהורה", ומאן דמוקי כתנאי — לא קפיד לשנות "טמאה". וא"ת: אכתי הויא מתני' כתנאי, דרישא דמתני' רבי עקיבא קתני לה, וסיפא דקתני "פולטת טהורה" — היינו דלא כר"ע דפליג בסמוך אר' אלעזר בן עזריה? וי"ל: דלא קפיד לאוקמי כתנאי אלא בתרי בבי דסמוכות זו אחר זו, אבל אההיא דריש פירקין, המרוחקות מההיא דפולטת, לא קפיד. וא"ת: למאן דתני "טהורה", טפי הוה ליה למנקט במתני' קרא ד"וקדשתם היום ומחר" (שמות ינו), דמשמע כרבי אלעזר בן עזריה? ואומר ר"י: דניחא ליה לאתויי "היו נכונים לשלשת ימים", דמוכח דמשום פליטת זרע הקפיד, דכתיב ביה "אל תגשו אל אשה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:3:1.english: He teaches in the first clause: "[Ritually] pure," and establishes it, etc. - Rabbi Yitzchak says that [the Gemara] does not emend [the Mishnah] to teach "ritually pure" [merely] in order to establish the entire [Mishnah] in accordance with Rabbi Elazar [ben Azarya]; rather, even without that, there are those who teach "ritually pure" and there are those who teach "ritually impure." Therefore, one who does not establish [the Mishnah] as [reflecting differing] Tannaim prefers to teach like those who teach "ritually pure," whereas one who establishes [it] as [reflecting differing] Tannaim is not concerned about teaching "ritually impure." And if you ask: Still, the Mishnah reflects [differing] Tannaim, for Rabbi Akiva teaches the beginning of the Mishnah [i.e., of this chapter], whereas the latter clause that teaches "[a woman who] discharges [semen on the third day] is ritually pure" is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who disagrees shortly [below] with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya? And one can answer: [The Gemara] is only concerned about establishing [the Mishnah] as [reflecting differing] Tannaim in the case of two clauses that are adjacent to one another; however, regarding that [clause] at the beginning of our chapter, which is distant from that [clause] of "one who discharges," it is not concerned. And if you ask: According to the one who teaches "ritually pure," it would have been more fitting to cite in the Mishnah the verse "and sanctify them today and tomorrow" (Exodus 19:10), which implies [the view of] Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya? And Rabbi Yitzchak says: It is preferable to him [i.e., the Tanna of the Mishnah] to cite "prepare yourselves for three days" [Exodus 19:15], because it proves that [Scripture] was concerned [specifically] about the discharge of semen, as it is written in it, "do not approach a woman."

Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:4:1.hebrew: פעמים שהן ד' כו' - במלתא דרבי אלעזר בן עזריה, ה"מ נמי לשנות בענין זה: "פעמים שהן שתים, פעמים שהן ג' כו'"; אלא להכי נקט ר' ישמעאל, משום דסבר ברביעי עבוד פרישה כרבי עקיבא, ובעונות לא בעי למתלי כמו שתולה רבי עקיבא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:4:1.english: "Sometimes there are four [periods], etc." - Regarding the statement of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, [the Tanna] could also have taught in this manner: "Sometimes there are two [periods], sometimes there are three [periods], etc." Rather, this is why [the Baraita] specifically cited Rabbi Yishmael: because he holds that they separated on the fourth [day], like Rabbi Akiva, yet he does not wish to make [the calculation] dependent on [a fixed number of twelve-hour] periods as Rabbi Akiva makes [it] dependent.

Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:5:1.english: "He ascended early in the morning" - [He] is speaking according to Rabbi Akiva.

Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:7:1.hebrew: ישראל קדושים הן כו' - ובלאו הכי היו פורשין, דאמר: "בוזה דרכיו ימות — זה המשמש מטתו ביום". ועוד, דקראן קדושים: "ואתם תהיו לי ממלכת כהנים וגוי קדוש":
Tosafot on Shabbat 86a:7:1.english: The Jewish people are holy, etc. - And even without this [command], they would have abstained, for [the Gemara] says: "He who despises his ways shall die — this [refers to] one who has marital relations during the day." And furthermore, because [Scripture] called them holy: "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation."
